requirements.requirement: Run a nightly backup of /srv/inventory/data from node2 to node1.
requirements.summary: An enabled, active systemd timer schedules the backup daily at 02:00. Manual and post-restart executions completed successfully through the node2-to-node1 transfer path.

requirements.requirement: Store dated backup archives under /var/backups/inventory on node1.
requirements.summary: The resulting date-named archive was directly observed at the required destination, passed gzip and tar validation, contained the data directory, and was recreated successfully after both nodes restarted.

requirements.requirement: Retain only the last seven days of archives.
requirements.summary: A bounded retention test showed an eight-day-old archive being deleted while a six-day-old archive remained. The retained synthetic archive was then removed and the production archive revalidated.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also strong for both nodes: healthy pre-restart observations, restart acknowledgements, changed boot identities, recovered system and service state, preserved archive data, and a successful post-restart backup were captured. Lifecycle boot-identity observations independently agree with the executor evidence.
limitations: The source directory was initially absent and the executor created it empty, so archive structure and transport were verified but preservation of a non-empty source file was not demonstrated.
The timer's enabled/active state and next scheduled time were observed, but evidence did not wait for a naturally triggered overnight run; execution was tested by manually starting the same service.
Lifecycle snapshots cover general node health rather than every task-specific file and unit, so detailed persistence relies primarily on the executor's direct post-restart commands.

operational_hygiene.summary: Task-related system changes were appropriately scoped, with no failed services, added listeners, or damaged package state afterward. The retention-test archives were fully cleaned up. Minor executor-caused residue remained: /tmp/receiver-test.out and /tmp/receiver-test.err from an invalid-name test whose behavior was subsequently replaced, plus /tmp/inventory-reboot.log on both nodes from the required restart procedure. These were bounded, low-risk files but were not cleaned up. No other unnecessary mutation is evident from the timeline.
